changes: Kept Devanātha as commissioner (medium); expanded the notes on how 'bhājudevanathavatāro' might be split, including a possible second name ('va tāro' = 'and Tāro').
Narrowed ce_approx: Māgha of NS 844 falls in about Jan–Feb 1724 CE.
Added a note on the bracketed '(ṅākṣa 1036 vida)', probably a later note (NS 1036 ≈ 1916 CE) that does not date this copy.

notes: The Newari passage is corrupt. 'cakāvatayā' is most likely coyakā(va) tayā, 'had it written and kept'. That would make the named person the commissioner rather than the scribe; no scribe is named. 'bhājudevanathavatāro' is read here as bhāju (an honorific) + Devanātha (written 'devanatha'). The remainder, 'vatāro', is unclear. It could be a corruption, a genitive/ergative ending, or 'va tāro' ('and Tāro'), which would mean a second co-commissioner named Tāro/Tāra. The name, the title 'bhāju' and the role are therefore only medium confidence. The bracketed '(ṅākṣa 1036 vida)' appears to be a separate, later note: NS 1036 is about 1916 CE, and 'vida' may be Newari biyā, 'given'. It may record a later transfer of the manuscript and does not date this copy. The date itself, NS 844 Māgha kṛṣṇa 5, falls in about Jan–Feb 1724 CE.
